title: Justice Department Files to Intervene and Dismiss Lawsuit that Would Hamper America’s AI Innovation and Security

reading.body:
The failure recorded here is not in the power plant and not in the lawsuit. It is in the summarization step of the pipeline that produced this incident record. A model was given source documents and returned an apology, a claim that the material was a corrupted or improperly formatted PDF, and a request for readable text. That output was then stored as the incident's summary. The claim is contradicted by the record itself, which carries legible titles for all five sources. This is a model asserting something false about its own input, and a pipeline publishing that assertion as a description of the documents.

The documents are a notice of intent to sue under the Clean Air Act over gas turbines powering a data center, a complaint filed by the NAACP and others, a Justice Department filing to intervene and dismiss, and news reports on pollution from the project. A summarizer that cannot read its input should fail visibly rather than emit prose. Catching this would have taken a check that the output actually describes the input, or a human review of the field before it was published.

What is not established: the notice of intent to sue is not a finding of violation, the complaint is an allegation, and the Justice Department filing is a motion, not a ruling. Nothing in the record shows why the model produced the message it did.
